item.title: European air traffic is targeted by new threats after a week of hoaxes
item.description: Officials across Europe reported a fresh slew of bomb threats against multiple flights on Friday, following a string of hoaxes that have caused flight diversions this week. Two broadcasters also received security threats.

item.title: The leader of a Kenyan doomsday cult is sentenced to 200 years in prison
item.description: Cult leader Paul Mackenzie was convicted of murdering 190 children and one adult after he ordered his followers to starve themselves to death in order to meet Jesus.

item.title: Hiring jumps: The economy added 165,000 jobs last month
item.description: The U.S. job market improved last month, according to a report from the Labor Department Friday. Employers added more jobs than forecasters had expected and the unemployment rate dipped to 4.1%.
item.content:encoded:

item.description: A judge has blocked construction of Trump's arch moments after it won federal approval to proceed. And, the Labor Department is set to release the latest jobs report today, a day after stocks plunged.

item.title: Why gold prices are surprisingly low
item.description: Gold tends to go up when there's uncertainty in the economy. For a while, the price reflected that. But this week, it dropped from a nearly $5,600 in January to below $4,000. What's going on?

item.title: Past White House adviser Raj Panjabi has written a playbook for 'living room' crises
item.description: Dr. Raj Panjabi is the author of Safer: A Playbook. His goal is to help people face a personal crisis — health, workplace, family conflicts — and "turn fear into action."

item.title: Why public schools nationwide are facing a massive drop in student enrollment
item.description: School enrollment was already expected to plunge by 2 million kids by 2030. Education experts say deporting immigrant families, many with school-age children, is making the crisis worse.
